definition: Probity means honesty and integrity proven over time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word probity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know probity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The referee's forty-year reputation for probity ended every argument on the pitch: if she called it out, it was out.
Honesty is telling the truth when asked; probity is a whole career of it, provable in the ledgers.
Integrity is moral wholeness you claim for yourself; probity goes a step further - integrity so tested and documented that the auditors vouch for it.

Uprightness is firm, visible adherence to what is right — a moral posture others can watch you hold. Probity adds proof across time: not just standing straight today, but a documented record of honest dealing that auditors and courts can verify.

Rectitude is strict correctness of principle — doing the right thing because the rule demands it, every time. Probity cares less about the rule than about the record: integrity demonstrated over years of dealings, the kind a career of clean ledgers proves.

When flood-relief money poured into the district, every faction demanded oversight of the fund — and then, unexpectedly, agreed on a single name.
Amara Sow had notarized the district's contracts for twenty-two years.
Her office kept carbon copies of everything; her fee book balanced to the franc; two audits, ordered by rivals hoping to ruin her, had ended by praising her instead.
What the factions trusted was not charm or eloquence.
It was probity — honest dealing with a paper trail, integrity that strangers could verify without taking anyone's word.
She ran the fund as she ran her office: receipts posted weekly, in the market square, where anyone could read them.
Years later, opponents still argued about the flood.
No one argued about the books.
